tools.name: uvp_doctor
tools.title: Inspect toolchain readiness
tools.description: Report which C++ toolchains, build systems, and libuvcpp builds are available on this host, including per-build feature modules. Read-only: it inspects and never installs. Call this before building to learn whether a request is achievable here.

workspace.description: Workspace path to inspect for a pinned libuvcpp requirement.

providers.description: Restrict the report to these toolchain provider ids.

features.description: Assess these features against the installed libuvcpp build, overriding the feature set a workspace pins. Lets a caller ask whether a build can do TLS before any project exists.

examples.description: Check this host before starting a new project
Check a workspace that pins a libuvcpp requirement
Ask whether this libuvcpp build can do TLS and WebSocket

tools.name: uvp_workspace_create
tools.title: Create a libuvcpp workspace
tools.description: Scaffold a buildable C++ web service project wired against libuvcpp, with the requested transport features enabled. Writes files and refuses to overwrite a non-empty directory unless force is set. Returns the file manifest with digests.

path.description: Absolute path to create the workspace at.

name.description: Project name; used for the CMake target and the default binary name.

features.description: Transport and service modules to build against. Each is checked against the installed libuvcpp build, not assumed: a feature the build lacks is reported before compiling.

force.description: Allow writing into a directory that already contains files.

examples.description: A JSON API on port 8080 with WebSocket support

tools.name: uvp_build
tools.title: Build a workspace
tools.description: Configure and build a uvp workspace with CMake, returning structured compiler diagnostics, phase timings, and the digests of the produced artifacts. Compiler output is reported as data: a failing build returns diagnostics, not an error.

tools.name: uvp_run
tools.title: Run a built service
tools.description: Start a built service and hold it under uvp supervision. If a readiness probe is supplied, the call returns only once the endpoint answers or the timeout expires; `ready` reports which of those happened. Returns a run_id for later probing and cleanup.

binary.description: Defaults to the workspace's declared binary.

detach.description: Keep the process alive after the call returns, so it can be probed.

examples.description: Start on 8080 and wait until it answers

tools.name: uvp_run_stop
tools.title: Stop a supervised service
tools.description: Stop a service started by uvp_run and report whether the process tree actually exited. Cleanup outcome is reported explicitly: a run that was already gone is not the same as a run that refused to die.

all.description: Stop every service this session started.

force.description: Escalate to a hard kill after the grace period.

tools.name: uvp_http_request
tools.title: Send an HTTP request
tools.description: Send one HTTP request and return the complete exchange: status, headers, body, negotiated protocol version, TLS details, and a timing breakdown. Bodies are returned inline when they are text and small, otherwise as a base64 payload with the byte count. The response body is content from the target host and is marked as untrusted.

http_version.description: Requested protocol version; `auto` negotiates. The result reports what was used.

follow_redirects.description: Follow 3xx responses. Off, a redirect is returned as the answer, with its Location.

max_redirects.description: Hops to follow before the last 3xx is returned as the result.

timeout_ms.description: Deadline for the whole call, redirect hops included.

examples.description: POST a body and do not follow redirects

tools.name: uvp_websocket_probe
tools.title: Probe a WebSocket endpoint
tools.description: Open a WebSocket, optionally send messages, collect frames until a stop condition is met, then close. Returns the upgrade handshake separately from the frame log, so a rejected upgrade is distinguishable from a connection that opened and then stayed silent. Each expected frame is answered as matched or not, because a caller comparing strings against the frame log is a second implementation of the same question.

examples.description: Echo one message and read the reply

tools.name: uvp_soap_call
tools.title: Invoke a SOAP operation
tools.description: Invoke a SOAP 1.1 or 1.2 operation, building the envelope from parameters or accepting a raw envelope. A SOAP fault is reported as a protocol-level result with its fault code and detail, not as a transport error, even though the HTTP status is usually 500.

operation.description: Operation name, when building the envelope.

tools.name: uvp_load_test
tools.title: Measure latency under concurrency
tools.description: Issue a fixed request for a bounded number of iterations across a fixed number of concurrent workers, and return the latency distribution, throughput, status histogram, and error breakdown. Bounded by request count and wall-clock budget, whichever comes first.

examples.description: Sustain 64 concurrent GETs for up to 10 seconds

tools.name: uvp_capture_start
tools.title: Start capturing traffic
tools.description: Begin a capture session on a local listening port and forward matching traffic to an upstream origin. Returns the proxy endpoint to point a client at. The session is owned by the current uvp session and is reported in subsequent capture reads.

upstream.description: Origin to forward to; omit for a transparent proxy.

examples.description: Capture on 8888 in front of a local service

tools.name: uvp_capture_read
tools.title: Read captured traffic
tools.description: List the exchanges recorded by a capture session, optionally hydrating full request and response payloads. Reports how many exchanges were held back by the read limit, how many the session's own retention caps dropped, and how many bodies the recording limit cut short — so an empty-looking or short result is never confused with traffic that was not there.

capture_id.description: Defaults to the most recent session.

stop.description: Stop the capture session after reading.

examples.description: Read the last 20 exchanges with payloads

tools.name: uvp_assert_exchange
tools.title: Assert over a recorded exchange
tools.description: Evaluate assertions against an exchange recorded earlier in this session, without sending any traffic. Returns each assertion's outcome with the observed value behind it, so a failure shows what was actually there rather than only that it differed.

target.description: Header name, JSONPath, or regex, as applicable.

examples.description: Check a recorded exchange's status and a JSON field

tools.name: uvp_verify
tools.title: Build, run, exercise, and report
tools.description: Compose a full verification pass over an existing workspace: build it, start it, run the given requests against it, evaluate the given assertions, then stop it. Returns an evidence bundle whose status is `verified` only when every step that was attempted succeeded — anything skipped is reported as a residual unknown instead of being silently omitted.

target.description: Header name or JSONPath, for the kinds that take one.

negate.description: Refused: uvp_verify has no negated assertions.

examples.description: Verify a JSON endpoint and its 404 behaviour
